O.location: plot area, May category at far right
O.content: The dark-red bar attached to "May" is much shorter on the page than every other displayed bar.
The title reads "Monthly Reservoir Release Volume"; the horizontal axis is inscribed "Month" and the vertical axis is inscribed "Release volume (m3)".

B.text: If the bars encode monthly release volume, May is a low-release case relative to the displayed months; absent a stated critical threshold or anomaly policy, the chart alone does not establish whether standard follow-up rather than escalation is required.
B.conditions: Applies when routing requires an explicit threshold or policy beyond relative comparison.

O.location: plot area, May category at far right
O.content: The bar attached to "May" is the shortest displayed bar and lies near the broken baseline.

B.text: Background filing is appropriate only when May is not a low-release case requiring active routing; a visibly minimal May bar would not support that condition if the chart encodes release volume.
B.conditions: Applies if filing excludes low-release cases needing follow-up.

O.location: plot area, May category at far right
O.content: The dark-red bar attached to the x-axis label "May" is much shorter on the page than every other displayed bar.

O.location: left vertical axis and plot area
O.content: The vertical axis is inscribed "Release volume (m3)" and has visible labeled ticks from "10,000" through "40,000".
The top of the May bar lies below the visible 10,000 tick and near the broken baseline.

B.text: If the bars encode monthly reservoir release volume on the common vertical axis, and the reporting workflow treats a month visibly far below all other displayed months as a critical low-release anomaly, then that month should be escalated. This severity convention is assumed because no explicit routing threshold is printed.
B.conditions: Applies to the displayed months and only if relative extremity is an accepted critical-anomaly criterion.
